feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 6 reproduced iteration 1 exactly (score 324.07, oval finish 0.70), so the stable base is a deterministic reference. I am keeping the controller unchanged from iteration 1, which the evidence supports. What I had to compensate for: the controller is tuned to a 0.12 m track and 0.8 kg. Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.10 m with kp scaled to 4.5) cut oval finishes to 0.10, and iteration 4 (0.6 kg) and iteration 5 (0.7 kg) cut them to 0.30 and 0.15 with oscillation up to about 0.32. So mass and track are tied to grip and yaw response at this gain. Iteration 2 showed that 16 mm sensors collapsed oval finishes to 0.00, so keep 12 mm. The s-bend and slalom max_error stays at about 0.064 m across all these geometries, above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Only a sensor position change has not been tested yet, so that is the open question. Depending on the next race: if the oval finish rate is about 0.5 or more with oscillation at or below about 0.3, hold this geometry as the stable base. If the oval finish rate is well below 0.5, treat iteration 1 as partly seed luck and judge future changes on a multi-seed average. Do not spend a run on sensor size, track or mass again.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration 1 geometry as the stable base if the oval finish rate is about 0.5 or more with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3, since iteration 6 reproduced it exactly.

If you want to address the s-bend and slalom max_error (about 0.064 m) with geometry, test one change only: a forward sensor offset of y = 0.06 m with the widened x = -0.024 to +0.024 m row, keeping 12 mm sensors, wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.8 kg.
Do not change sensor_size from 0.012 m, reduce wheel_track below 0.12 m, or move mass below 0.8 kg again. Iterations 2, 3, 4 and 5 all lowered the oval finish rate.
